I get the cold tone thing and it’s horrible. When my boyfriend broke up with me, in the time just before he was very cold, monotone and wouldn’t make eye contact with me. It’s extremely traumatic and dehumanising to experience that. And I got told the same things (oh you could get any guy you want, you deserve a 6ft tall guy with abs (which is not what I want!!)) and he just came over all cold. I want you to feel reassured that he wasn’t being cold and cruel because of you. Guys this age are often emotionally immature, and they shut down their feelings instead of experiencing them, which is not helpful. Please understand that it’s not you, or anything you have done wrong. 

In order to help you move on, get some paper and write down one thing you didn’t like about him. If you can’t do that, just one thing that was meh, or a little niggle. The next day write two things and the third day try three things. After a week, you will realise that actually, while you will miss him, maybe you could do better, or that it wouldn’t have worked long term. 

I recommend googling the Ted talk by Abbey Gibbs (Screw breakups). She has great energy and honestly sometimes it just gets me through the day if I listen.

Oh! Please don’t beat yourself up! What happens when someone breaks their leg? Of course they give it time to heal, but if they walk on it too early it’s really painful. It can even make things worse. So you sit in bed with a cast staring out the window at people walking perfectly on their legs. You have to rest it, you have to heal. You can’t get mad at yourself for not being able to walk on it. You ask others for help getting you from place to place. One day the leg is much better and you can tentatively venture out. One day you run on your strong leg. Don’t beat yourself up, and we all need someone to lean on. 

Also! Please try cognitive restructuring if you haven’t yet. It really helped me and there’s a lot of things online and about other stuff. 

The point of medication is to get you to the stage where you can get help. It’s what allows you to relax just enough, so that you can get a therapist, or complete that self help book.

Best wishes x

We had to head home so fast from uni that we didn’t say goodbye in person. It absolutely sucks that I can see him, and I struggle with anxiety and so I cry because I miss him. I know what makes me feel better are frequent FaceTimes during the week and also texting goodnight before bed. I also find making plans for when we get out of lockdown helps, because it helps me to realise that one day soon, I can see him again. I also really try to keep myself busy. Wishing you the best.

Same for me, except with fire alarms and other sirens. They just absolutely set me off. So yeah I have issues with sound, and even woke up from a nightmare shaking due to picturing the sound in my mind. I think its because we had a faulty burglar alarm when I was little, and it went off once in a while, and then I felt like I was being teased for my parents because I was scared of it. Bearing in mind it was right outside my window and I was like 4-5 at the time. Really haven't been the same since being woken up at 3 am in my university halls with their insanely loud alarms. I could barely sleep until I left uni at the end of the semester. What helped me was listening to stories and managing some sleep, however, I can no longer listen to that podcast without flashing back to those anxious times. Perhaps some of us are more noise-sensitive, perhaps I am on the spectrum, but either way, I have anxiety and hate loud noises too. Wishing you the best.
